method: Code and specification trace of Home's 'what next' resolution ladder (nextAction and focusPlan in js/modules/hub.js), subjects registry (js/core/subjects.js), and domain study/practice engines (js/core/ja.js, js/core/jasrs.js, js/core/code.js, js/core/mind.js, js/core/creatives.js, js/core/money.js).
observed: Home's Up Next card relies on nextAction() (lines 657-713) and focusPlan() (lines 754-893). nextAction checks running focus, KOS.srs.dueCount() (which only checks srs.js curriculum/custom cards, ignoring Japanese FSRS facets in jaSrs/state.ja.reviews and Code retrieval cards), countdowns, pacing (exam subjects only), daily directives (todo.autoItems), and store.state.ui.lastRef iterated across SUBJECTS in fixed order (['compsci', 'maths', 'it', 'code', 'ja', 'mind', 'creatives']). Money is not in SUBJECTS at all. For Code, Japanese, Mind, and Creatives, any progress, due reviews, practice sessions, or tasks are completely ignored by rungs 1-4. Even in rung 5 ('Where you left off'), it navigates via KOS.show('ref', { subject, ref }) rather than their native pages (#/code, #/japanese/session, etc.), and prioritizes compsci/maths/it whenever any lastRef exists for them. focusPlan() similarly only schedules calendar study blocks, exams, assignments, or pacing, with no representation of Code capstones/retrieval, Japanese kana/SRS/path, Mind practice, Creatives projects/drills, or Money budgets.
evidence: js/modules/hub.js:657-713 (nextAction), js/modules/hub.js:754-893 (focusPlan), js/modules/hub.js:1213-1291 (paintUpNext), js/core/subjects.js:23-44 (SUBJECTS definition: exam vs non-exam, money excluded), js/core/srs.js:410-441 (dueCount ignores state.ja and state.code).
contraryEvidence: js/modules/hub.js:1560-1570 includes Code, Japanese, Mind, and Creatives under the 'Continue' desks section at the bottom of the page once started (e.g. KOS.ja.started()), but this is a static navigation list of desk cards, not the 'Up next' / 'What should I do next' decision engine.
alsoAffects: iPad, desktop, mobile; user onboarding and daily task guidance across all non-exam domains.

method: Code and specification trace comparing Home's weekly study hours calculation (hoursOn / weekH in js/modules/hub.js) against Reports' studied metric calculation (study in js/core/report.js and reports.js).
observed: Home computes weekly study hours via hoursOn(iso) (js/modules/hub.js:917-920), which sums duration over all sessions in KOS.sessions.all() where s.type !== 'media'. This includes focus timer sessions, quizzes, flashcards, due-reviews, exam practice, Japanese sessions, and tracker entries. Conversely, Reports calculates its headline 'Studied' tile (js/core/report.js:187-193 and js/modules/reports.js:723, 758, 1112) strictly from sessions where focusE = e.type === 'focus'. All non-focus study sessions (quizzes, flashcards, exams, reviews) increment reviews, quizzes, or exams counts, but their durations are completely omitted from s.mins. For a user who spends substantial time in flashcards, quizzes, and Japanese reviews alongside modest focus blocks, Home reports e.g. 12h14m while Reports' 'Studied' tile displays 2h32m for the exact same week.
evidence: js/modules/hub.js:917-920 (hoursOn), js/modules/hub.js:1463-1465 (weekH), js/core/report.js:114-117 (isStudy), js/core/report.js:187-193 (focusE gate for mins), js/modules/reports.js:723, 758, 1112 (tile('Studied', W.hm(s.mins), ...)).
contraryEvidence: js/core/report.js:114-117 defines isStudy(e) to include all non-media, non-todo sessions, but inside study(), line 190 explicitly gates mins += mm behind if (focusE). This reflects an internal contradiction within report.js itself.
alsoAffects: Weekly, monthly, term, and annual report summaries across all devices; analytics trust.

method: Code trace of streak milestone award logic in js/core/governor.js:329-339 and streak calculation in js/core/sessions.js:166-176 across multi-day session sequences.
observed: In js/core/governor.js:330-338, milestone bonuses check if (stk >= ms && g.milestones[key] !== KOS.srs.addDays(KOS.srs.todayISO(), -(stk - ms))). In js/core/sessions.js:166-175, streak(sid) starts its cursor at addDays(today, -1) whenever today has no completed study activity yet (hasStreakActivity(today, null) is false). Consequently, before the first study session of the day, when any non-study session is logged (such as ticking a reminder, habit, or todo directive via KOS.sessions.log({ type: 'todo' })), stk evaluates to yesterday's streak (e.g. 7). The expression addDays(todayISO(), -(stk - ms)) evaluates using today's date rather than yesterday's, computing a target date shifted 1 day forward compared to what was saved yesterday. Since g.milestones[key] was recorded as yesterday's date, the inequality test evaluates to true, awarding gold and XP again and saving the shifted date. Once the user later completes a study session today, stk increments to 8, shifting the target date back to match yesterday's date, which triggers another mismatch against the newly saved date, paying the milestone bonus a second time on the same day.
evidence: js/core/governor.js:329-339 (streak milestone awarding loop), js/core/sessions.js:166-176 (streak function and yesterday cursor fallback), js/core/governor.js:278 (todo session invokes milestone checks).
contraryEvidence: None; the comment at line 335 claims it is 'keyed to the run's start date so a fresh run re-earns the bonus', but the math formula addDays(todayISO(), -(stk - ms)) depends directly on todayISO() without accounting for whether stk was computed ending today or ending yesterday.
alsoAffects: Governor economy (gold and XP inflation), all devices, daily engagement rewards.

method: Code trace of narrative template generation in js/core/reportwords.js (largestShare, template, longTemplate) and report persistence in js/core/reportstore.js.
observed: In js/core/reportwords.js:17-18, SUBJECT is hardcoded as { compsci: 'Computer Science', maths: 'Maths', it: 'IT' } and SUBJECT_SHORT as { compsci: 'CS', maths: 'Maths', it: 'IT' }. In largestShare(s) (lines 45-50), s.bySubject includes all tracked study spaces where focus sessions occurred ('code', 'ja', 'mind', 'creatives'). When any of these subjects has the greatest focus minutes, top is set to that subject's ID. In template() (line 140) and longTemplate() (line 93), the narrative interpolates SUBJECT[top]. Because 'code', 'ja', 'mind', and 'creatives' are missing from SUBJECT, SUBJECT[top] evaluates to undefined, producing sentences like 'undefined took the largest share, 3h 20m of 4h 00m, across 4 sessions on 3 of 7 days' or 'All 4h 00m went to undefined, across 4 sessions.' When reports are generated and persisted via js/core/reportstore.js:221-226, 279-280, template narrative is permanently stored in IndexedDB and replicated to Supabase.
evidence: js/core/reportwords.js:17-18 (hardcoded SUBJECT map missing non-exam subjects), js/core/reportwords.js:45-50 (largestShare), js/core/reportwords.js:136-141 (template week narrative interpolation), js/core/reportwords.js:90-94 (longTemplate month/term/year narrative), js/core/reportstore.js:221-226 (immutable report persistence).
contraryEvidence: js/core/subjects.js:54 provides KOS.subjects.name(id) which safely maps all 7 subjects, but reportwords.js bypassed KOS.subjects and defined its own private 3-subject lookup table.
alsoAffects: Weekly, monthly, term, and annual report cards, export share cards (js/modules/reportshare.js), cloud replication, all devices.

method: Code trace of Hero Daily Goal directive rendering in js/modules/hub.js:1154-1173, tick handler in js/modules/todo.js:53-69, and session award in js/core/governor.js:278.
observed: In js/modules/hub.js:1162-1170, daily goal items from KOS.todo.autoItems() are rendered as checkable buttons with onclick: function () { KOS.todo.setChecked(a.key, !on, a.label); KOS.rerender(); }. In js/modules/todo.js:62-68, when val is true, setChecked immediately executes KOS.sessions.log({ type: 'todo', metrics: { item: label } }) without requiring any evidence that the underlying task (e.g. review backlog, exam revision, study block) was performed. Furthermore, when unticked (val is false), line 66 simply executes delete t.autoChecked[today + '|' + key]; store.save(); without rolling back or recording a penalty for the previously logged award. Re-ticking calls KOS.sessions.log again, paying +5 XP, +1 gold, and +2 HP via governor.js:278 on every tick cycle infinitely.
evidence: js/modules/hub.js:1162-1170 (Hero directive button click handler), js/modules/todo.js:56-69 (setChecked logging todo session and deleting check state without rollback), js/core/governor.js:278 (unconditional award for e.type === 'todo'), AGENTS.md (Domain rule: 'One deliberate action earns at most one reward event').
contraryEvidence: Lines 1121-1140 render 'Today's three' when enabled by homeThree(), which uses tickThree(p). However, when 'Today's three' is not present, lines 1154-1173 unconditionally render the fallback autoItems() directive list with the defective setChecked toggle.
alsoAffects: Level progression, gold balances, Governor integrity, all devices.

method: Code trace of Japanese lesson check calculation (evidence and syncChecks in js/core/ja.js), review recording (record and finishSession in js/core/ja.js), and inspector rendering in js/modules/jatopic.js.
observed: In js/core/ja.js:116, the four lesson checks are ['Read the notes', 'Heard every example', 'Passed the practice', 'Held in reviews']. Check 4 requires all lesson items to have facets held in reviews (items.length > 0 && held === items.length). In js/core/ja.js, syncChecks(id) writes ev.checks to the persistent progress record via store.setCheck(SID, id, i, on). However, syncChecks is only invoked in markPage (line 106), markHeard (line 112), and finishLesson (line 241). In record() (lines 177-191) and finishSession() (lines 220-230), where review facets are graded and stability updated, syncChecks is never called. Consequently, p.check[3] is never written to store.state.progress['ja:' + id]. While jatopic.js:293 dynamically calculates KOS.ja.evidence(ref) in the inspector (showing 3/4 · 75% prior to holding, or even 4/4 if held), the stored progress record never receives check 4. Because store.setCheck only transitions status to 'done' when all 4 checks are stored (p.check.every(Boolean) in js/core/store.js:459), stored status remains 'started', preventing the spine and unit counts from reflecting lesson completion.
evidence: js/core/ja.js:116-146 (CHECKS, evidence, syncChecks), js/core/ja.js:177-191 (record lacks syncChecks), js/core/ja.js:220-230 (finishSession lacks syncChecks), js/core/store.js:455-467 (setCheck status transition requiring all checks), js/modules/jatopic.js:292-328 (inspector dynamic read vs stored status).
contraryEvidence: code.js:724 explicitly calls (cd.concepts || []).forEach(function (c) { var c0 = concept(c); if (c0) syncChecks(c0.lesson); }); when retrieval cards are reviewed. This reveals that the Japanese domain omitted the analogous review synchronization that Code implemented.
alsoAffects: Spine progress indicators, stage/unit completion tallies, dashboard stats, all devices.

method: Code trace of Japanese runner lifecycle in js/modules/jarun.js (mount, run, leave, end) and session logging in js/core/ja.js:218-230 (finishSession).
observed: In js/modules/jarun.js, each answered exercise immediately updates and saves facet intervals via KOS.ja.record(ex.key, res) (lines 419-420). However, session finalization (KOS.ja.finishSession(results, ...)), which awards XP/gold and logs the activity via KOS.sessions.log({ type: 'ja', ... }), is encapsulated exclusively within end(early) (lines 432-450). end() is only called when completing all items (line 410) or by clicking the in-runner exit button ('✕' / leave(), line 394). There are no unmount lifecycle callbacks, popstate listeners, pagehide, or beforeunload handlers attached to the runner or router. If a user navigates away via the sidebar rail, bottom mobile navigation bar, browser Back button, iPad edge swipe gesture, or page refresh, the runner DOM element is discarded without end() being invoked. Consequently, all answered items remain rescheduled into future dates, but finishSession is never executed: no session is logged to store.state.sessions, no XP/gold is awarded, and the daily study streak activity is lost.
evidence: js/modules/jarun.js:392-407 (header '✕' button and leave()), js/modules/jarun.js:417-431 (mount callback storing results locally), js/modules/jarun.js:432-450 (end() executing finishSession), js/core/ja.js:220-230 (finishSession performing sessions.log), js/core/router.js:260-295 (router view replacement without unmount lifecycle hooks).
contraryEvidence: leave() prompts with KOS.ui.confirm if results exist, but this only guards clicking the runner's internal '✕' button, leaving all external browser/system/shell navigation paths unguarded.
alsoAffects: Mobile, iPad, desktop; streak continuity, Governor rewards, user trust when multitasking.

method: Layout, DOM, and CSS trace of .k-topic-tabrow in js/modules/hub.js:2623-2652, 2745-2750, css/views/study.css:208-219, css/views/japanese.css:304, and js/modules/jatopic.js:83-91.
observed: In js/modules/hub.js:2746, the topic tab row .k-topic-tabrow contains: .k-scroller (wrapping tabBar), moreSlot, workBtn ('✎ Working'), editBtn ('✎ Edit'), and cx ? cx.modeSwitch() : null ('Learn | Reference' segmented control). In css/views/study.css:208-212, .k-topic-tabrow is a flex container where .k-scroller has flex: 1 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0; and all other children have flex: none;. In css/views/japanese.css:304, .k-ja-mode has margin-inline-start: auto; with no responsive hiding or width constraint. On an iPhone (viewport width 375px to 390px), after accounting for container padding, the fixed-width sibling controls (workBtn ~85px, editBtn ~65px, .k-ja-mode ~160px, plus flex gaps) occupy ~350px. This leaves virtually zero width for .k-scroller, which collapses to ~5px due to min-inline-size: 0. Furthermore, hub.js:2624 disables the '+N' folding menu on phones (max-width: 700px), expecting all tabs to scroll horizontally. Within the 5px collapsed scroller, Notes, Practice, Reviews, and Files tabs are completely hidden by overflow. Because the Practice session is accessed via the Practice tab (jatopic.js:101, 110), users on iPhone cannot launch the practice session from the lesson.
evidence: js/modules/hub.js:2745-2750 (k-topic-tabrow structure), css/views/study.css:208-212 (flex: none on siblings, min-inline-size: 0 on scroller), css/views/japanese.css:304 (.k-ja-mode), js/modules/hub.js:2623-2634 (phone tier disables '+N' fold), js/modules/jatopic.js:97-105 (Practice tab definition).
contraryEvidence: Standard curriculum topics lack cx.modeSwitch(), so their non-scroller controls fit within phone viewports without crushing the scroller. The issue is unique to Japanese (and contexts adding extra inline segmented controls without responsive wrapping).
alsoAffects: iPhone users, small mobile viewports (<=420px), Japanese lesson navigation and practice access.

method: Code trace of CSV header detection in js/core/money.js:970-984 (guessMapping, GUESS) and import validation in js/modules/money.js:937-940.
observed: In js/core/money.js:970-977, column header regexes are: amount: /^(amount|value|amount \(gbp\)|transaction amount)$/i, out: /^(paid out|money out|debit|withdrawals?|out)$/i, in: /^(paid in|money in|credit|deposits?|in)$/i, and payee: /^(description|payee|merchant|name|counter party|details|reference)$/i. Santander midata CSV exports specifically use 'Merchant/Description' for payees and 'Debit/Credit' for transactions. The combined compound headers fail every regex pattern in GUESS because of the slash separator and combined keywords. In js/modules/money.js:937-940, the file validation logic specifies: if (mapping.date == null || (mapping.amount == null && mapping.out == null && mapping.in == null)) { fail('It has no header row with a date and an amount.'); return; }. Because 'Debit/Credit' is not matched to amount, out, or in, the CSV import fails immediately with this error, completely blocking Santander midata files from being imported.
evidence: js/core/money.js:970-977 (GUESS regex patterns), js/core/money.js:978-984 (guessMapping), js/modules/money.js:937-940 (header validation failure condition).
contraryEvidence: Users could manually edit the CSV file in a text editor to rename headers prior to uploading, but the app provides no manual column-mapping fallback interface when auto-guessing fails.
alsoAffects: All devices, UK banking data import (Santander personal/business midata standard).

method: Code trace of CSV parsing and delimiter detection in js/core/money.js:947-969 (parseCSV) and header mapping in js/modules/money.js:937-940.
observed: In js/core/money.js:947-969, parseCSV samples only the very first line of the file to determine the delimiter: var sample = text.split(/\r?\n/)[0] || ''; var delim = (sample.match(/;/g) || []).length > (sample.match(/,/g) || []).length ? ';' : .... If a file begins with a leading blank line, sample is empty, causing delimiter detection to default to comma , and completely failing semicolon-delimited files. Furthermore, line 968 hardcodes header: rows[0] || []. If an Online Banking CSV includes an account preamble (such as bank name, account number, sort code, or opening balance on lines 1-3 before the table header), rows[0] is assigned the preamble row. When guessMapping(parsed.header) runs on this preamble, it finds no matching date or amount headers. Line 938 of js/modules/money.js then triggers fail('It has no header row with a date and an amount.'), aborting the import. There is no preamble scanning or header row heuristic.
evidence: js/core/money.js:948-950 (delimiter detection on line 0 only), js/core/money.js:968 (header: rows[0]), js/modules/money.js:937-940 (guess(parsed.header) failing when header is a preamble or unparsed line).
contraryEvidence: Files with clean, preamble-free RFC 4180 comma-delimited headers parse properly; the defect is specific to bank exports with preambles, leading blank lines, or European/midata semicolon formats with leading whitespace.
alsoAffects: All devices; imports from major UK and European banks (Barclays, Nationwide, Santander, HSBC) that include statement header blocks.
